A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzyme from lactating mammary gland has a molecular weight of 260,000 and a subunit of 110,000.
the purified enzyme from lactating rabbit mammary gland has a molecular weight of approx. 250000 and a sedimentation coefficient (S20, w) of 7.0.
the purified acetyl-CoA carboxylase had a molecular mass of 240000, a subunit mass of 24000, a pH optimum of 7.5, a K(m) for acetyl-CoA of 0.15 mM and a K(m) of 0.25 mM for ATP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a method for purifying rabbit mammary gland acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
the purified enzyme from rabbit mammary-gland was similar in many respects to the enzyme from other tissues.
we have shown the feasibility of using a simple, inexpensive spectrophotometric method for the assay of acetyl-CoA carboxylase in crude tissue extracts.
